entities.name: Umar al-Aqta
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
“Umar al-Aqta, also known as Amer or Ambros in Byzantine sources, was a semi-independent Arab emir of Malatya (Melitene) from the 830s until his death in the Battle of Lalakaon on 3 September 863.

   As a key figure in the Byzantine Empire's eastern frontier, Umar al-Aqta played a pivotal role in the struggles for control of the region.

   His legacy can be seen in the many Arabic and Turkish epic stories that emerged in the centuries following his death, cementing his place in the annals of history as a prominent figure in the region's cultural heritage.

   With his military prowess and strategic alliances, Umar al-Aqta left an indelible mark on the region, one that continues to be felt to this day.
